Oct 14, 2026

Rebuilding the river trail bridge

The footbridge over the river trail closed in August after an inspection found rot in two of its main beams. Crews spent the last six weeks lifting the deck in sections, replacing the beams with laminated timber, and bolting new steel plates where the old ones had rusted through.

Underneath the deck they also found a beaver lodge built against the east abutment. The regional wildlife officer asked the crew to leave it in place, so the new abutment was poured a metre further back and the approach path now curves around it.

The bridge reopens to walkers and cyclists on Saturday morning. The parks department asks riders to dismount on the deck for the first two weeks while the new surface cures, and says the lights along the approach will be switched on before the end of the month.
